title: Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite expected to miss rest of season, ending World Cup hope
content:
Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite is expected to miss the remainder of the season, ending his hopes of making England’s World Cup squad.

Tests early this week confirmed the 23-year-old had sustained damage to his right hamstring in Sunday’s 2-1 Merseyside derby defeat by Liverpool.

Branthwaite was in tears as he was taken off on a stretcher in the 87th minute, and was later seen leaving Hill Dickinson Stadium on crutches. Everton manager David Moyes later told reporters that he was “worried” about the central defender’s injury.

There are indications Branthwaite’s injury is not quite as bad as first feared. It is hoped he will return to play a part in Everton’s pre-season preparations, sources briefed on the injury said, but that will depend on him avoiding further setbacks.

Moyes has looked to manage Branthwaite’s minutes in recent months, in an attempt to avoid another costly injury setback.

The central defender spent the first half of the campaign on the sidelines with a hamstring injury and underwent surgery in October following what Everton described as a “complication” in his rehabilitation. Branthwaite also missed the recent warm-weather training camp in Portugal as a precaution. He has played just 10 Premier League games this season, seven of which were starts.

Everton face West Ham United at the London Stadium on Saturday.

Branthwaite’s absence for the remainder of the season represents a major blow to Everton’s hopes of qualifying for Europe. Despite Sunday’s derby loss, Moyes’ side are just one point off sixth-place Chelsea with five games to play.

They are heavily reliant on the former Carlisle United man’s recovery pace and his ability to play out of defence on his left foot. There is a case that he is the side’s most important player tactically, given he facilitates a move to a more aggressive, front-foot style of play.

Experienced defender Michael Keane is the most likely replacement for Branthwaite, but a further injury in central defence would almost certainly prompt a reshuffle, with right-back Jake O’Brien shifting inside and one of Seamus Coleman, Nathan Patterson or James Garner taking his place.

Branthwaite was always seen as an outside bet for an England World Cup place under Thomas Tuchel. Even when fit, he has found himself behind the likes of Newcastle United’s Dan Burn and Ezri Konsa of Aston Villa in the pecking order.

After returning in January, he had hoped to stake a late claim for Tuchel’s squad. “That was my aim at the start of the season,” he told reporters earlier this year. “It’s going to be difficult.

“I haven’t (spoken to Tuchel). I’ve been out for so long and haven’t played much football, so it’s down to me, and my performances, to give myself the best possible chance to be in and around it.”
